newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan said seeking $500 million against remittances.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan said seeking $500 million against remittances.

text.p: The Pakistani government is seeking to raise $500 million against securitisation of expatriate workers' remittances estimated at around $1.5 billion a year, brokers and bankers said on Tuesday.
They said the government had asked nine short-listed foreign and local banks and brokerage houses to present their proposals for final selection to act as lead managers for the issue.
"The government is seeking a five- to seven-year maturity fund of $500 million against remittances now estimated at around $1.5 billion," said a foreign banker who asked not to be named.
He said the short-listed firms would present their proposals to the Finance Ministry on Thursday and Friday.
He said the government had set a target for the delivery of the funds by the end of September to meet its foreign debt repayment schedule.
Bankers say a recent three-year $300 million Eurobond issue lead by ANZ Grindlays Bank has encouraged Pakistan to seek more funds from international markets.
